# Judges Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_281.jpg, JDG_page_282.jpg

1. And the men of Ephrayim were called together, and they crossed over to Tsaphon. And they said to Yiphtach, "Why did you cross over to fight against the sons of Ammon and did not call us to go with you? We will burn your house over you with fire."

2. And Yiphtach said to them, "A man of great strife I was — I and my people — with the sons of Ammon greatly. And I called you, and you did not save me from their hand.

3. And I saw that you were not saving, and I put my life in my palm and I crossed over against the sons of Ammon, and YHWH gave them into my hand. And why have you come up to me this day to fight against me?"

4. And Yiphtach gathered all the men of Gil'ad and fought with Ephrayim. And the men of Gil'ad struck Ephrayim, because they said, "Fugitives of Ephrayim [are] you, Gil'adites, in the midst of Ephrayim, in the midst of M'nashsheh."

5. And Gil'ad captured the fords of the Yarden against Ephrayim. And it was, when the fugitives of Ephrayim said, "Let me cross over," the men of Gil'ad said to him, "Are you an Ephraimite?" And he said, "No."

6. And they said to him, "Say now 'Shibbolet.'" And he said "Sibbolet," and was not able to speak correctly. And they seized him and slaughtered him at the fords of the Yarden. And there fell at that time of Ephrayim forty-two thousand.

7. And Yiphtach judged Yisrael six years. And Yiphtach the Gil'adite died and was buried in the cities of Gil'ad.

8. And after him Ivtsan of Beit-Lechem judged Yisrael.

9. And he had thirty sons. And thirty daughters he sent outside, and thirty daughters he brought in for his sons from outside. And he judged Yisrael seven years.

10. And Ivtsan died and was buried in Beit-Lechem.

11. And after him Elon the Z'vulunite judged Yisrael. And he judged Yisrael ten years.

12. And Elon the Z'vulunite died and was buried in Ayyalon in the land of Z'vulun.

13. And after him Avdon son of Hillel the Pir'athonite judged Yisrael.

14. And he had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys. And he judged Yisrael eight years.

15. And Avdon son of Hillel the Pir'athonite died and was buried in Pir'athon in the land of Ephrayim, in the hill-country of the Amalekite.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **v.6 — "Shibbolet"/"Sibbolet":** The most famous linguistic test in history. The Gileadite shin (שׁ) was pronounced as a sibilant that Ephraimites could not reproduce — they said samekh (ס) instead. This is the origin of the English word "shibboleth."

2. **v.3 — "I put my life in my palm":** va'asimah nafshi v'khappi — an idiom for risking one's life. Literally "I placed my soul in my hand" — as though one's life were a fragile object held in an open palm.

— EMET, AI Translator
